claims.text: Solutionizing, quenching, and aging at 700°C for 2 hours will precipitate fine, coherent Ni3Ti nanoparticles.
The Ni3Ti-forming aging treatment will improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties relative to the unaged material.
The proposed alloy contains approximately 40 at.% Ti and 40 at.% Ni, with the remaining approximately 20 at.% evenly distributed among Cr, V, and Al.
The proposed composition meets the requirement that every constituent be present at 5–35 at.%.
Solution treatment homogenizes the alloy microstructure.
The specified treatment produces a uniform dispersion of nanoscale, coherent Ni3Ti precipitates in the matrix.
Nanoscale Ni3Ti precipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by Ni3Ti precipitates increases elevated-temperature yield strength.
Ni3Ti precipitation strengthening improves creep resistance at elevated temperature.
At 650°C, the aged alloy will have at least 20% greater yield strength than the solutionized-and-quenched baseline.
The aged alloy will have improved high-temperature stability.
The solutionized-and-quenched baseline has a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure without strengthening precipitates.
The Ni3Ti precipitates are stable at service temperatures around 650°C.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may coarsen the Ni3Ti precipitates.
Coarsening of the Ni3Ti precipitates could reduce their strengthening benefit.

contradictions.description: The alloy is specified as approximately 40 at.% Ti and 40 at.% Ni while also being claimed to satisfy a 5–35 at.% limit for every element. Both primary constituents exceed the stated 35 at.% maximum.
